output.summary: KEP-784 proposes graduating kube-proxy's component configuration to beta through a series of alpha config versions, ending with the last alpha being copied as v1beta1. It restructures the flat KubeProxyConfiguration into clearer sections (platform, root, backend).
output.rationale: The flat v1alpha1 kube-proxy config grew over time and mixed instance-local with shared options, platform-specific with generic options, and backend-specific with agnostic options, making it hard to use and maintain. The KEP proposes to graduate it in small steps over at least one release cycle, with each step producing an alpha version. The current status is implementable at stage alpha, so the graduation to beta has not yet happened.

alternatives.option: Keep the flat v1alpha1 configuration format unchanged
alternatives.why_not: The readme says the flat format made the configuration both hard to use and to maintain, so a plan to restructure and stabilize it is needed.

alternatives.option: Graduate to beta in a single step
alternatives.why_not: The readme says the graduation is to be done in small steps across at least one Kubernetes release cycle, with one or more alpha versions before v1beta1.

evidence.quote: Clearly, this made the configuration both hard to use and to maintain. Therefore, a plan to restructure and stabilize the config format is needed.
The idea is to conduct the process of graduation to beta in small steps in the span of at least one Kubernetes release cycle.
This will be done by creating one or more alpha versions of the config with the last alpha version being copied as v1beta1 after the community is happy with it.
